verification.date_context: read-only re-audit of finding gateway-1 (X-Request-ID collides with unique call_logs.request_id, poisoning batched audit inserts) as filed by another auditor
verification.primary_fix_site: backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go:84 (client-controlled value) + backend/internal/model/model.go:248 (uniqueIndex on it) + backend/internal/audit/audit.go:67-70 (whole-flush discard); fixing any one of the three breaks the chain, the discard handler is the minimum fix
files_read_end_to_end: backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go (831 lines, whole file incl. AuthMiddleware :189-231, shouldAuditCall :253-267, writeLog :270-281, Handle :298-478, forward :489-551, forwardStream :619-771)
backend/internal/db/db.go (73 lines, whole file - GORM config, AutoMigrate, dialect support)
backend/internal/admin/routes.go (196 lines, whole file - route/auth surface, no call-log delete endpoint)
backend/internal/admin/audit.go (204 lines, whole file - list/detail/export read paths)
backend/internal/admin/auditws.go (120 lines, whole file - live view)

finding.title: Client-controlled X-Request-ID collides with unique call_logs.request_id, poisoning batched audit inserts (cross-tenant audit destruction)
finding.evidence: gateway.go:84 `if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.GetHeader("X-Request-ID")); v != "" && len(v) <= 128 {` -> gateway.go:306 `reqID := resolveRequestID(c)` -> gateway.go:311 `requestID: reqID,` -> gateway.go:272 `RequestID: p.requestID,` -> model.go:248 `RequestID string `gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40" json:"request_id"``. audit.go:67-70 `if err := l.db.CreateInBatches(batch, 50).Error; err != nil {` / `log.Printf("[audit] batch insert failed: %v", err)` / `}` / `batch = batch[:0]`. Flush triggers: audit.go:60 `ticker := time.NewTicker(200 * time.Millisecond)`, audit.go:62 `batch := make([]*model.CallLog, 0, 64)`, audit.go:79 `if len(batch) >= 64 {`. Queue-full fallback audit.go:44 `l.db.Create(cl)` (return value discarded) under the comment audit.go:35 `队列满时直接落库兜底（不丢审计）`. Live broadcast audit.go:46 `l.broadcastLive(cl)` -> hub consumed by admin/auditws.go:72 `msgs, cancel := s.al.Broadcaster().Subscribe()`.
finding.impact: Any holder of one enabled gateway API key can reuse a single fixed X-Request-ID. The first such row persists; every later row with that ID violates the UNIQUE index, which aborts the ENTIRE chunked INSERT and, because GORM wraps a >50-row flush in a transaction, the entire flush - silently destroying co-flushed call audit for every other API key on the gateway. At a sustained rate of >=5 requests/second (one per 200 ms tick) essentially every flush contains a poisoned row, so gateway-wide call auditing goes to zero for the duration. The attacker simultaneously evades persisted auditing of its own later calls (only the stale first-wins row is visible), and token/billing/dashboard aggregates that read call_logs (admin/tokenstats.go:138-237, admin/dashboard.go:23-27, admin/models.go:202-205) understate traffic. The 128-byte header limit vs the size:40 column additionally fails the whole flush on MySQL(strict)/PostgreSQL deployments without needing any duplicate at all; on SQLite it stores unbounded until retention cleanup.
finding.recommendation: Server-generate the audit row's request_id (keep the client X-Request-ID in a separate non-unique column, e.g. client_request_id), or on unique/constraint failure fall back to per-row inserts and retry the remaining rows; never discard the batch. Enforce the 40-char limit (and an allowlist charset) in resolveRequestID.
finding.mitigations_checked: No insert-with-ignore/ON CONFLICT clause; no per-row retry; no dedup window; metrics ring is capped (metrics.go:77-79) so only the audit path is poisoned. Disabled/expired-key and XFF spoofing separately verified safe.

reason.1_evidence_integrity_every_quote_verifie: Every cited fragment was read in situ and matches byte-for-byte. gateway.go:84 is exactly `if v := strings.TrimSpace(c.GetHeader("X-Request-ID")); v != "" && len(v) <= 128 {` inside resolveRequestID (gateway.go:83-88), whose only other branch is `return newRequestID()` (:87). gateway.go:306 `reqID := resolveRequestID(c)`; gateway.go:308 `c.Header("X-Request-ID", reqID)`; gateway.go:311 `requestID: reqID, start: start, keyID: apiKey.ID, keyLabel: apiKey.Name,` (finding quotes the `requestID: reqID` prefix - accurate fragment); the value reaches the model unchanged at gateway.go:272 `RequestID: p.requestID,`. model.go:248 is exactly `RequestID string `gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40" json:"request_id"``. audit.go:67/68/70/79/60/62/44/46 all exact (67 `if err := l.db.CreateInBatches(batch, 50).Error; err != nil {`, 68 `log.Printf("[audit] batch insert failed: %v", err)`, 70 `batch = batch[:0]`, 79 `if len(batch) >= 64 {`, 60 `ticker := time.NewTicker(200 * time.Millisecond)`, 62 `batch := make([]*model.CallLog, 0, 64)`, 44 `l.db.Create(cl)`, 46 `l.broadcastLive(cl)`). metrics.go:77-79 is `if len(mt.recent) > 50 { mt.recent = mt.recent[len(mt.recent)-50:] }`, so the ring-cap aside is also correct. No wrong-line, no missing quote.
reason.2_the_index_really_exists_and_really_is_: AutoMigrate runs over model.AllModels() (db.go:63 `if err := gdb.AutoMigrate(model.AllModels()...); err != nil {`) and AllModels includes `&CallLog{}` (model.go:301), so the `uniqueIndex` tag is materialised as `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON call_logs(request_id)` on first start for all three supported dialects (db.go:25-41). The gateway never supplies a per-key or per-request discriminator (gateway.go:272 is the sole assignment; gateway.go:306 is the sole generation point), and gateway_test.go:164 `if got := resolveRequestID(mk("trace-abc-123")); got != "trace-abc-123" {` documents that the header is returned verbatim - arbitrary attacker-chosen strings, no charset allowlist. Every CallLog row carries a non-empty RequestID, so empty-string/NULL exemption does not save it either (and two empty IDs would collide just the same).
reason.3_one_row_per_request_so_the_attacker_mu: Checked for a self-collision shortcut and found none: the only audit writer is writeLog, called from exactly one place - the deferred closure in Handle (gateway.go:314-319 `defer func() { if shouldAuditCall(snap.General, ap.status) { s.writeLog(ap) } ... }()`), and `ap` is one struct per request, so retries/failover (gateway.go:447-471) and forwardStream do not emit a second row. The collision therefore genuinely requires the attacker to repeat the header across requests, which is exactly what the finding claims ('reuse one fixed X-Request-ID header').
reason.4_mechanism_confirmed_empirically_with_t: The finding blames SQLite's whole-statement abort. That is true, and it understates the blast radius: with 51..64 rows in a flush, gorm v1.25.12 finisher_api.go:57-60 `if tx.SkipDefaultTransaction || reflectLen <= batchSize { tx.AddError(callFc(tx.Session(&Session{}))) } else { tx.AddError(tx.Transaction(callFc)) }` wraps the 50+14 chunks in an outer transaction (SkipDefaultTransaction is never set - db.go:42-46 passes only Logger and TranslateError), so the first chunk that had ALREADY been inserted is rolled back too. audit.go:67 discards the returned error into a log line and audit.go:70 resets the buffer unconditionally: nothing retries, nothing re-queues. Probe (identical glebarez/sqlite v1.11.0 + gorm v1.25.12 + TranslateError:true + the verbatim `uniqueIndex;size:40` tag; source at %TEMP%\dshprobe\main.go, run with go1.24.4/GOTOOLCHAIN=local against the repo's module cache): (A) 64-row flush with a duplicate at index 63 -> error `duplicated key not allowed`, total rows afterwards = 1 (the pre-existing seed only), victims persisted 0/63; (B) 40-row single-statement flush with the duplicate at index 20 -> victims persisted 0/39 (SQLite ABORT rolls back the whole multi-row INSERT); (C) 30-row flush containing the duplicate pair, no pre-existing row -> victims persisted 0/28 and both attacker rows lost as well. Every persisted-row outcome matches the finding's claim.
reason.5_queue_full_and_live_view_claims_verifi: audit.go:41-46 shows the fallback `default: l.db.Create(cl)` with the *gorm.DB return thrown away, then an unconditional `l.broadcastLive(cl)`. Probe (E) confirms a duplicate single-row Create returns `duplicated key not allowed` and persists nothing, so the 'do not lose audit' comment at audit.go:35 is falsified on this input class. broadcastLive (:50-57) publishes whatever is marshalled from the in-memory row, and admin/auditws.go:72 streams that hub to the console, so the WS view keeps showing calls that never reach the DB - the divergence the finding relies on for 'not obviously noticed' is real. Also note the broadcast fires on ENQUEUE, i.e. strictly before the flush attempt, so the divergence is structural, not only in the queue-full case.
reason.6_input_is_untrusted_and_the_attacker_la: Reachability: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses and /v1/messages all sit behind gws.AuthMiddleware() (admin/routes.go:27-31), whose only requirement is an enabled API key (gateway.go:215-221) plus the key's own IP allowlist (:222). Nothing anywhere normalises, hashes, salts or namespaced-prefixes the header, and no CORS/proxy layer in this codebase strips it. Destructive capability is genuinely new: there is NO call-log delete/purge endpoint for any role (admin/routes.go:111-115 expose only GET list/detail/export; the sole DELETE-ish path is the hourly retention sweep audit.go:102 `l.db.Where("created_at < ?", cutoff).Delete(&model.CallLog{})`, reachable by nobody). Before this bug a tenant could at worst write unbounded rows of its OWN; now it can erase other tenants' rows. So the 'attacker already has the privilege' refutation does not apply.
reason.7_attack_cost_is_lower_than_filed_zero_t: The finding implies a normal traffic pattern; in fact the cheapest poison costs nothing. The header is consumed at gateway.go:306 before the body is even parsed, and the audit write is deferred (gateway.go:314-319) with shouldAuditCall returning true for any non-ok status (gateway.go:257 `if status != "ok" { return true }`) regardless of CallAuditOnlyErrors/sampling, while CallAuditEnabled defaults true (settings.go:33 `CallAuditEnabled: true, CallAuditSampling: 1}`). So `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `-d '{'` returns 400 at gateway.go:328-332 (before alias resolution, rate limiting, quota and any upstream call - the early returns precede steps 3/4/5 at :410 and :419), and still writes an audit row carrying the attacker's fixed ID. Rate limiting (gateway.go:410) and quota (:419) are never consulted on that path, so the default rule set cannot throttle the poison. This strengthens, not weakens, the finding.
reason.8_blast_radius_and_persistence: Per flush at most 64 rows are lost (audit.go:62 cap, :79 threshold), but flushes happen every 200 ms (:60) and the batch is global to all keys and all requests (single writer goroutine started at audit.go:31), so loss is not confined to the attacker's traffic. Sustained >=5 req/s guarantees at least one poisoned row in virtually every flush -> near-total gateway audit blindness for as long as the attack runs, with the only operator-visible trace being a stderr line (audit.go:68) that no admin API, WebSocket, Prometheus metric (metrics.go has no insert-failure counter) or console view surfaces. Recovery of the poisoned ID is not automatic either: the seed row survives (retention sweep at 90 days default, settings.go:31), and even if it is deleted, the attacker's next request re-seeds and conflicts resume. Collateral integrity damage is broader than the audit table read path: token/billing dashboards are computed from call_logs (admin/tokenstats.go:138/143/192/207/237, admin/dashboard.go:23-27, admin/models.go:202-205), so the same act silently deflates per-model and per-key usage evidence.
reason.9_the_size_40_vs_128_sub_claim_is_accura: gateway.go:84 admits up to 128 bytes into a column tagged size:40. Probe (D) confirms SQLite stores the 128-byte value untruncated (no insert failure, unbounded growth until the hourly retention sweep), so the finding is right that on SQLite this half is a storage/portability issue rather than an extra kill vector - and right that on other dialects it is one: db.go:28-39 supports postgres and mysql, where GORM emits character varying(40)/varchar(40), so a 41..128-byte ID fails the statement with value-too-long (PostgreSQL always; MySQL under default strict sql_mode) and takes the whole flush down with no duplicate required. Stated as dialect-conditional inference (not tested here), that is a legitimate amplification, and the finding flagged it as such. On MySQL non-strict, silent truncation to 40 chars would instead make distinct >40-byte client IDs collide with each other - the same poisoning, without any header reuse.
reason.10_mitigation_search_nothing_else_breaks: Repo-wide grep for `OnConflict|ErrDuplicatedKey|Ignore\(|Clauses\(` under backend/ returns zero hits, so no upsert/insert-or-ignore anywhere; no dedup window; no per-row retry; no panic-recovery in the writer (audit.go:30-33 starts writerLoop with a plain `go`, not util.SafeGo) that would help since GORM returns errors rather than panicking. The one true partial mitigation is that the attacker's own later rows are also dropped (first-wins), so a tenant poisoning the audit also loses its own persisted trail - which the finding correctly reframes as evasion-through-collision, since the surviving first-wins row is a stale, benign-looking decoy that admin/audit.go:68 `s.db.Where("request_id = ?, reqID).First(&r)` happily returns for any query on that ID.
reason.11_severity_calibration: Not critical: the actor is an authenticated gateway tenant (valid enabled sk- key), the effect is integrity/availability of audit data rather than unauthenticated RCE, authz bypass or data exfiltration, and no read primitive over other tenants' content is granted. Not medium: this is not a hardening nicety - it is an actively exploitable, essentially free, self-masking cross-tenant destruction of the security-logging control (the project's own REQ-015/REQ-001 retention promise) with no log-level trace an operator would see, plus a forensics-evasion primitive for the attacker's own calls. That is squarely the filed 'authed-but-severe' band -> high stands.
reason.12_adjacent_observation_not_scored_here: While reading the request path I noticed admin/server.go:108-115 `func clientIP(c *gin.Context) string { if v := c.GetHeader("X-Forwarded-For"); v != "" {` takes XFF unconditionally for the OperationLog.IP attribution, bypassing the TRUSTED_PROXIES stance enforced at main.go:92 - i.e. admin operation-audit IPs are client-spoofable. That is an admin-domain issue, out of scope for this verdict and not counted in it.

exploit_sketch:
Attacker precondition: possession of ONE enabled gateway API key (gateway.go:202-228). No model access, no quota headroom, no reachable upstream, no tokens spent.

1) SEED (one request, costs nothing): `curl -X POST http://gw:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-<own-key>' -H 'X-Request-ID: healthcheck-0001' -d '{'` -> gateway.go:84 accepts the header verbatim; the malformed body returns 400 at gateway.go:328-332 BEFORE rate limit (:410), quota (:419) and any upstream call, yet the deferred audit at gateway.go:314-319 still writes the row because shouldAuditCall is always true for status != "ok" (gateway.go:257) with CallAuditEnabled defaulting true (settings.go:33). That row lands in the next 200 ms flush and persists: call_logs.request_id = 'healthcheck-0001'.
2) POISON: repeat step 1 forever with the same X-Request-ID. Each new row now collides with the seed, so audit.go:67 returns `duplicated key not allowed`, audit.go:68 prints one stderr line, and audit.go:70 throws away every queued row in that flush - all of them other tenants' calls. Probe scenario A/B/C: 0/63, 0/39, 0/28 co-flushed victim rows survive; scenario A additionally loses the 50-row chunk that had already been inserted, because gorm finisher_api.go:57-60 wraps 51..64-row flushes in a transaction.
3) BLIND THE GATEWAY: at >=5 poisoned requests/second (one per tick of audit.go:60) every flush carries a collision, so gateway-wide call audit stops persisting entirely for the attack's duration - while the single writer goroutine keeps running (audit.go:63-71 never returns) so nothing crashes, no error reaches any API/metric, and victims see normal 200 responses.
4) EVADE + DECOY: the attacker's own poisoned calls are never persisted, and GET /api/admin/v1/audit/calls/healthcheck-0001 (routes.go:112 -> admin/audit.go:65-71 `First(&r)`) returns only the stale first request it planted - a benign-looking row for an ID under its control - while CSV export (admin/audit.go:95-110) and token-stats (admin/tokenstats.go) silently understate everything. The live console keeps showing traffic because audit.go:46 `l.broadcastLive(cl)` pushes to the hub admin/auditws.go:72 subscribes to regardless of persistence, so an operator watching /audit/ws sees the destroyed calls as 'handled'.
5) DIALECT VARIANT (no collision needed): on a PostgreSQL/strict-MySQL deployment (db.go:28-39) send `X-Request-ID` of 41..128 bytes; the value passes gateway.go:84 but exceeds the `size:40` column (model.go:248), the INSERT fails with value-too-long, and the whole flush is discarded the same way. On SQLite that same request simply stores 128 bytes unbounded until the hourly retention sweep (audit.go:102).

empirical_verification.harness: Standalone Go program (outside the repo, no source file touched) replicating audit.go's writer semantics: glebarez/sqlite v1.11.0 + gorm.io/gorm v1.25.12 (the exact versions in backend/go.mod), gorm.Config{TranslateError: true} per db.go:42-46 with SkipDefaultTransaction left false, AutoMigrate of a struct carrying the verbatim tag `gorm:"uniqueIndex;size:40"` from model.go:248, and CreateInBatches(batch, 50) per audit.go:67. run with go1.24.4 / GOTOOLCHAIN=local / GOPROXY=file://$GOMODCACHE/cache/download.
results: A: 64-row flush, seed row pre-existing, duplicate at index 63 -> err 'duplicated key not allowed'; total rows in DB after = 1 (seed only); victims persisted 0/63.
B: 40-row flush (single multi-row INSERT), duplicate at index 20 -> victims persisted 0/39 (SQLite ABORT unwinds the whole statement).
C: 30-row flush containing the duplicate pair with no prior row -> victims persisted 0/28; both attacker rows lost too.
D: 128-byte request_id -> insert succeeds on SQLite and stores 128 chars untruncated (VARCHAR(40) is advisory there).
E: single-row fallback Create on a duplicate -> returns 'duplicated key not allowed', row not persisted; Write() discards the error (audit.go:44).

mitigations_confirmed_present: The attacker cannot pre-empt someone else's identifier space blindly at scale beyond a fixed string it chooses itself; collisions with legitimately-generated IDs are impossible in practice because newRequestID() emits 32 hex chars (gateway.go:75-79) and a client ID that is not an exact string match of the attacker's seed does not collide.

No read primitive is granted: destroying rows does not let the attacker read other tenants' input_text/output_text; list/detail/export (admin/audit.go:49-110) are all behind s.AuthMiddleware() JWT (routes.go:111-115).

No other persistence path is poisoned by the same header: metrics are in-memory with a 50-entry ring (metrics.go:76-79), quota consumption goes through qm.Consume (gateway.go:614, :768) not call_logs, and APIKey.last_used_at updates are per-key (gateway.go:247).
The single-row queue-full fallback still persists non-duplicate rows (probe E: only the duplicate fails), so the discard is scoped to collisions and to the affected flush.

The 128-byte cap in gateway.go:84 does bound the oversized-value growth per row, and the writer goroutine never dies on an error (audit.go:63-71), so the damage is data loss, not a crash/DoS of the request path.
Header length 41..128 causes no insert failure on the default SQLite deployment (probe D), so the finding's own dialect scoping of that half is honest.
Retention sweep (audit.go:102) eventually removes the seed row, so a poisoned identifier is not permanently immutably locked - though it re-seeds on the attacker's next request.
mitigations_absent: No ON CONFLICT / clause.OnConflict / INSERT OR IGNORE anywhere (repo-wide grep: zero hits), so a unique violation is a hard statement error.
No per-row fallback, no retry, no partial-success accounting after audit.go:67; audit.go:70 `batch = batch[:0]` discards unconditionally on both success and failure paths.
No validation that the client-supplied X-Request-ID is unique-per-request, non-colliding, charset-safe, or <=40 chars (gateway.go:84 is the only check).

No separation between a server-generated audit key and a client-supplied correlation ID: the same string is used for the response header (:308), the upstream trace header (:514), the SSE writer (:629) and the unique DB index (:272).
No failure visibility: the discard is a log.Printf to stderr only (audit.go:68) - no metric, no admin API surface, no WS event, no alert, and the live view (audit.go:46) actively hides the gap.
No call-log delete endpoint or admin purge exists, so this is the only way a tenant-role actor can remove audit rows at all - confirming the privilege is new.
corrections_to_filed_text: Understatement fixed: the loss is not limited to 'a failed 50-row chunked INSERT'. For flushes of 51..64 rows (i.e. exactly the >=64 threshold the finding cites) GORM wraps the two chunks in a transaction (finisher_api.go:57-60), so the first 50-row chunk that had already been written is rolled back too - verified by probe A leaving 1 row (the seed) in the DB.

Attack cost fixed: the poison needs no successful model call at all. A 400 from gateway.go:328-332/348-362/370-376 still writes an audit row (gateway.go:257, settings.go:33) and bypasses rate limiting (gateway.go:410) and quota (gateway.go:419), so the default 5-req window rules cannot slow it.

Impact scope extended: destruction also corrupts the billing/usage evidence chain (admin/tokenstats.go, admin/dashboard.go, admin/models.go read call_logs), and the surviving first-wins row is a stale attacker-chosen decoy returned by /audit/calls/:request_id.

Cosmetic: gateway.go:311 was quoted as a fragment of a longer line; the primary cited line audit.go:67 needs no correction (mechanism sites: audit.go:70 for the discard, gateway.go:84 + model.go:248 for the root cause).
recommendation_verdict: Recommendation is correct and should be adopted as filed, with one prioritisation: the durable fix is to stop letting client input own a unique column - generate the persisted request_id server-side (newRequestID()) and store the client's X-Request-ID in a separate non-unique column (client_request_id, size:128, plus the 40->128 length agreement), which removes the whole class without touching the writer. Independent hardening that must also ship, because a unique index on any client-influenced column can recur: on constraint failure re-insert the flush row-by-row (or use clause.OnConflict{Columns: request_id, DoNothing/Replace}) instead of audit.go:70's unconditional discard, and surface a counter/alert so the loss is not stderr-only. Enforcing <=40 chars (and an [A-Za-z0-9._:-] allowlist) in resolveRequestID is cheap and closes the MySQL/Postgres variant. Note that keeping the client ID in the response header and the upstream trace header (gateway.go:308/:514) is fine - only the audit primary correlation should be server-generated.
